title: serving-runtime-version-governance-and-rollback-safeguards
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary: Define a pragmatic, operationally focused semantic versioning and LTS channel governance for the serving runtime that minimizes customer disruptions while allowing necessary breaking changes. This ticket captures the policy text, rollout gates, deprecation windows, and the upgrade/rollback tooling requirements for runtime teams and integrators.

Goals:
- Establish clear criteria for what counts as a breaking change vs. safe change (behavioral, wire/API, performance/latency, config semantics).
- Define LTS channel lifecycle and how we map minor/patch releases to fast and stable channels.
- Specify mandatory rollout gates (canary %, SLO health thresholds, regression guards) and automatic rollback triggers.
- Define developer-facing upgrade tooling surface (compatibility tests, migration helpers, upgrade CLI) and required QA artifacts for every release.

Policy highlights (proposal):
1) Versioning scheme: runtime MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (e.g., 2.4.1). MAJOR increments signal possibly incompatible runtime semantics or model artifact changes that may require user action. MINOR can include opt-in features and non-breaking defaults. PATCH is for bug fixes.

2) Breaking change criteria (require MAJOR bump):
- Any change that alters the persisted on-disk model or KV cache format without automatic migration.
- Removal or semantic change of an existing runtime API (REST/GRPC contract) that will cause client errors.
- Changes to default scheduling/routing that change latency expectations by >25% for tail latency at 99th percentile across benchmark suites.

3) Deprecations:
- Deprecation MUST be announced at least one MINOR release before removal with a clear migration path and automated compatibility tests.
- Standard deprecation window: 90 days / 3 minor releases (whichever is longer) before removal.

4) LTS & channel mapping:
- channels: edge, stable, lts-YYYYQ (quarterly named LTS).
- Edge receives MINOR/PATCH quickly for rapid iteration. Stable is a short-term guarded channel. LTS is a 12-month supported channel with security/backport policy.
- Backports: security/critical fixes accepted to active LTS branches only; feature backports discouraged.

5) Rollout gates and automation:
- Canary: 3-stage rollout: internal-only -> 5% external canary -> 25% ramp -> 100% if healthy.
- Metrics guards: error rate increase >0.5% absolute OR +50% relative on a primary error metric for two consecutive 5-minute windows triggers automatic rollback. Latency regression: >15% increase in p99 for two consecutive windows triggers halt and manual review.
- Integration tests: every release must run the compatibility matrix (old client/new runtime, new client/old runtime, old client/old runtime) across three representative models.

6) Upgrade tooling and artifacts (required for any MINOR/MAJOR release):
- Migration plan doc with step-by-step procedures and example curl/sdk commands.
- Automated migration scripts for on-disk formats or KV cache upgrades where possible.
- Upgrade CLI (runtime-upgrade) that validates pre-upgrade health checks and can orchestrate staged rollouts with canary percentages and rollback.
- Post-upgrade smoke tests and automated traffic-shifting playbook.

7) Rollback playbook:
- Playbook must include: immediate traffic-shift command, database/state rollback steps (if applicable), communication templates, and post-mortem schedule.
- Rollbacks must preserve audit logs and trace IDs for root-cause analysis.

8) Communication and docs:
- Release notes should include a compatibility section, required actions for customers, and an explicit deprecation timeline.
- Notify on-console and via email to active enterprise customers 14 days prior to MAJOR changes, and 72 hours for MINOR changes that change defaults.

Open questions (for PR review):
- Exact numeric thresholds for metric guards (proposal above is intentionally conservative).
- LTS support duration (proposal: 12 months) vs. enterprise SLA options.
- How strictly to enforce compatibility tests for low-usage internal models vs. public models.

Acceptance criteria:
- Written policy doc merged to Confluence and linked from internal release checklist.
- A GitHub PR that adds the release gating automation to the CI pipeline (canary orchestration + automatic rollback script).
- Implementation plan for the runtime-upgrade CLI scoped and scheduled.

Notes on trade-offs:
- Conservative rollback thresholds reduce blast radius but may slow feature rollout; recommend periodic tuning after 3 releases.
- Strong deprecation windows improve customer trust but increase maintenance burden.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: Finalize policy text and sign-off (this ticket).
- Week 2–3: Prototype rollout orchestration as a small service/helm job; CI hooks for canary.
- Week 4–6: Implement compatibility matrix tests in CI and add migration scripts for known format changes.
- Week 7: Pilot on internal cluster, iterate thresholds.
